label: Programme adoption boundary: classify the 1725 title copper
notes: 1724 has a different annual-memory frontispiece; 1725 has a catalogued title copper of unresolved identity; 1726 directly shows the Historia/Genealogia/Heraldica programme in Type A.
reopen_rule: Resolve with direct inspection of the opening leaves of BSB/MDZ bsb10428127 or another securely dated complete 1725 copy. Generic further web searching without a new image should not reopen the branch.

label: Type B entry and early Müller–Tyroff chronology, 1739–1740
notes: Type A is directly secure through 1738. A 1739 catalogue reads G. Müller del. / M. Tyroff sc.; British Museum object 1910,0906.2 catalogues a 1740 Historia Genealogia Heraldica frontispiece as Tyroff after Müller. Direct Type B is secure by 1744.
reopen_rule: Inspect 1739 and/or 1740 images directly, then compare composition, dimensions, lettering and stable defects with 1744/1746. Signatures alone are insufficient for design or matrix identity.

label: Type B to Type C design replacement boundary
notes: Direct photographed 1746 copy is Type B; archived 1747 frontispiece thumbnail is structurally Type C; 1748 institutional scan is Type C. The design-level replacement boundary is therefore fixed at 1746/1747.
reopen_rule: Reopen only if a securely dated 1747 copy shows a different frontispiece configuration, or if the archived thumbnail is demonstrated to be mispaired. Matrix identity within the transition remains a separate question.

label: Does late Type A recurrence represent the same physical matrix?
notes: Type A is directly controlled in the 1720s–1730s and reappears in 1759 and 1765 after Types B and C have circulated. This establishes repertoire/stock recurrence at design level, not one copperplate across four decades.
reopen_rule: Compare dimensions, plate marks, lettering, stable scratches/defects, wear and retouching across at least one early Type A impression and the 1759/1765 late impressions. No further design-level search is needed.

label: Type C matrix/state sequence and the fec. 1755 problem
notes: Type C is directly present by 1747 and in 1748, 1749, 1751, 1755, two 1756 copies, 1757, 1761 and 1763. Finna reads M. Turoff fec. 1755 on the 1762 frontispiece. The date must therefore be tested as a within-Type-C matrix/state event, not as the invention date of the design.
reopen_rule: Obtain high-resolution, copy-paired images for 1751/1755/1761/1762/1763 and compare the production line, frame, lettering, dimensions and stable defects. The 1762 image-to-Finna pairing is the first priority.

label: Late Seyfart/Raspe frontispiece persistence and copy divergence, 1767–1776
notes: Catalogue controls show copy-dependent late configurations: some multi-volume sets report repeated frontispieces, some collations do not count one, and a 1771 volume has a Titelkupfer. A ca.1773 market object may be a Clio-bearing Handbuch but host identification is unconfirmed.
reopen_rule: Inspect opening leaves of at least one secure 1767/1768 copy and the targeted 1773 BSB Handbuch bsb10428164. Record literal title page, frontispiece design, production signature and copy sequence. Do not create duplicate manual tasks beyond the existing M006/M007/M025 targets.

label: Publisher stock custody from Weigel through Tyroff and into later host regimes
notes: The 1766 Verlagskupfer preface directly proves a Weigel/Tyroff publishing environment in which old coppers were retained as publisher-held reusable capital. Firm succession evidence makes long-lived plate stock plausible, but direct custody of the Historia/Genealogia/Heraldica matrices across specific owners remains unproved.
reopen_rule: Require dated firm/estate/account/inventory evidence or matrix-level physical continuity linking the frontispiece stock. Do not infer custody solely from design recurrence or family succession.

label: Issue-level resolution of C. Weigels Witwe
notes: Current firm-succession evidence favours Magdalena Esther Weigel for the elder-Weigel Wappenkalender imprint, while some catalogues assign 1731–1735 records to Barbara Magdalena Weigel. Literal imprint and person resolution must remain separate.
reopen_rule: Only direct title-page, privilege, advertisement, account, or contemporary firm evidence tying a specific issue to one household should change the issue-level person resolution.

label: Final historiographical novelty boundary
notes: Araújo already closes broad novelty claims about title-page materiality, visual evidence, transmediation, Gatterer's evidentiary system and paratextual epistemology. The final sweep must test adjacent scholarship on seriality, print/publisher plate stock, heraldic/genealogical visual culture, copy-specific afterlives and the material history of frontispieces.
reopen_rule: Freeze after a dated web/library sweep identifies direct prior art and the remaining defensible object-scale claim. Reopen only for newly published scholarship or a newly identified directly overlapping study.
